c: Ironwood Auto Care, an independent repair shop with eight bays
s: Ironwood Auto Care gets many reviews that say the repairs were good but the experience was stressful. Customers say they were surprised by the final bill and felt their questions were brushed off.

The shop owner (judge) wants you to explain how a service advisor builds trust with customers who know little about cars, how to explain repair costs and policies, and how to handle a customer who is angry about a bill.
p: Build and maintain relationships with customers
Interpret business policies to customers/clients
Handle customer/client complaints
Respond to customer inquiries
Explain the role of customer service as a component of selling relationships
n: Explains problems in plain language and gives an estimate before work begins
States policy on approvals, warranties and payment clearly
Stays calm, acknowledges the issue and proposes a fair fix
Follows up after the repair to confirm satisfaction
q: A customer says the final bill is $200 more than the estimate. What do you say?
How do you explain a repair a customer does not seem to need right now?

c: Rev Detail Studio, a car detailing and paint protection business
s: Rev Detail Studio has strong reviews but few new customers. The owner wants to promote a new ceramic coating package without discounting heavily and would like to reach car enthusiasts and busy professionals.
The owner (judge) wants you to explain how to choose promotional channels, what messages will work for each audience, and how to coordinate the promotion.
p: Identify the elements of the promotional mix
Explain the nature of a promotional plan
Coordinate activities in the promotional mix
Explain the use of video/images for digital marketing
Describe referral programs that can be used to build brand/promote products
n: Uses advertising, social media, events, public relations and referrals
Sets goals, audience, message, budget and schedule
Before-and-after photos, short videos and a consistent look across channels
A referral reward leverages happy customers
q: How would you promote the package without lowering the price?
What would you do if a customer posts a negative review online?

c: Summit Auto Parts, a retail and online auto parts store
s: Summit Auto Parts sells everything from wiper blades to brake kits. Many do-it-yourself customers are unsure which part they need and some buy the wrong one and return it.

The sales manager (judge) wants you to explain how to acquire and use product information to sell, how to identify features and benefits, and how to recommend the right product for a first-time buyer.
p: Acquire product information for use in selling
Analyze product information to identify product features and benefits
Determine customer/client needs
Recommend specific product
Explain the nature and scope of the selling function
n: Uses catalogs, supplier training and online lookups to learn products
Translates features into benefits, such as longer life or easier installation
Asks vehicle make, model, year, use and budget
Recommends a specific product and checks fit before the sale
q: A customer wants the cheapest brake pads but drives a heavy truck. What do you say?
What do you do when you do not know the answer to a product question?

c: Quicklane Tire & Service, a tire shop with five locations
s: Quicklane Tire & Service has collected years of sales and service records, but no one has used the data. Customers come in for tires but rarely return for alignments or oil changes, and the company does not know why.
The marketing director (judge) wants you to explain how the company can use its information to understand customers, which reports would be useful, and how to turn findings into recommendations.
p: Apply marketing analytics
Provide sales analysis reports
Display data in charts/graphs or in tables
Leverage data to recommend personalized, relevant campaigns
Maintain security of marketing data
n: Looks at repeat visits, service mix, time between visits and customer segments
Reports on sales by service, location and month
Uses charts to make patterns easy to see
Sends reminders based on mileage or last service and protects customer data
q: What would you do if the data showed customers do not return because of a bad experience at one location?
How would you decide which customers to contact first?

c: Torque Fleet Services, which maintains delivery vehicles for local businesses
s: Torque Fleet Services tracks maintenance on 600 vehicles using spreadsheets and paper tickets. Some vehicles are overdue for service, and a recent breakdown cost a client a full day of deliveries.
The general manager (judge) wants you to explain how technology and information systems could help, which records the company should keep, and how it should keep client information safe.
p: Identify ways that technology impacts business
Explain the role of information systems
Describe the nature of business records
Monitor internal records for business information
Explain information privacy, security, and confidentiality considerations in business
n: Software with automatic service reminders and dashboards
Databases that centralize schedules, costs and repair history
Keeps accurate records of service, parts, warranty and client contacts
Uses access limits, backups and training to protect data
q: What would you do if your new system alerted you to more overdue vehicles than your mechanics could handle?
How would you convince technicians to use a new software system?
